SMTO-GML-0003 — That Gmail account name is already used by another entry

GUID: ecf31113-d773-49a5-8921-0689bcfa5e50
Slug: gmail-account-key-conflict
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save your Gmail sign-in under a name that already belongs to a different saved entry, such as another email address or another kind of account. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't overwrite it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store and search for the name you used, to see what is already saved under it. The existing entry belongs to a different account or type, and SMTO won't overwrite it.
  2. Ask SMTO to connect your Gmail account again and give it a name that isn't already in the Parameter Store list. A new name lets SMTO save this account without touching the other entry.
  3. Delete the old entry with Delete parameter only if you are sure nothing uses it any more; otherwise leave it as it is. Removing an entry that other tasks still use would break them.

What success looks like

  • A new Gmail entry with the right email address appears in Parameter Store, and the other entry is unchanged.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the other entry's value to make it match your Gmail account.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Parameter Store key chosen for the Gmail account already belongs to a different profile type, OAuth app or mailbox address, so the connect or token-save flow refused to overwrite it.

What this means

  • The selected storage key already belongs to another profile type, OAuth app or mailbox identity. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The selected storage key already belongs to another profile type, OAuth app or mailbox identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect existing profile type, app reference and mailbox email before choosing a key.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the Parameter Store account mappings and inspect the existing record at that key (profile_type, email, oauth_app_ref). Rerun the Gmail connect flow with a deliberately distinct, unused key; never reuse a stale key or overwrite another account's record.
  • Refresh Parameter Store account mappings and choose a distinct intended key.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended identity uses a deliberate distinct key without overwriting another account.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
